I’m farming only 13.1 mu, and there are just three of us at home, with some labor going off-farm, so I can’t spread myself too thin. I’ll keep the land in the same pattern that has been steady for me: most of it in wheat-maize double cropping, and a smaller piece in cotton. Wheat and maize are my main income safety net, and cotton gives me another source of cash if grain prices are weak. I finished okay last year with moderate fertilizer, so I won’t change too much. The extension man says not to push nitrogen blindly, but if I cut too hard and the crop turns weak, that loss is worse for me than spending a bit more. Still, water and fertilizer both cost money now, so I’ll stay around the middle of the local range, not the high end. For wheat I’ll do base fertilizer plus one topdress, and irrigate at the key stages if rainfall is short. Maize has to go in fast right after wheat harvest, so I’ll keep tillage simple and use a hybrid seed I can get locally. Cotton takes more hand work, so I’ll keep it on a smaller area and not expand it. With family labor limited, I need a plan I can actually finish on time, not one that only looks good on paper.
